title: What Local Citations Are and Why Inconsistent Ones Destroy Your Rankings

facts.fact: The page defines a local citation as any online mention of a business's Name, Address, and Phone number, collectively called NAP.
facts.quote: A local citation is any online mention of your business’s Name, Address, and Phone number, collectively known as NAP.

facts.fact: The page states that Google's local search algorithm is built around three core signals: relevance, distance, and prominence.
facts.quote: Google’s local search algorithm is built around three core signals: relevance, distance, and prominence.

facts.fact: The vendor states that setting up a Bing Places for Business listing takes about ten minutes.
facts.quote: It takes ten minutes to set up and is worth doing.

facts.fact: The page names three major data aggregators (Data Axle, Localeze, and Foursquare) that automatically distribute business information to hundreds of downstream directories.
facts.quote: are the three major data aggregators that automatically distribute business information to hundreds of downstream directories.

facts.fact: According to the page, Apple Maps pulls listing data from a combination of its own data and Yelp feeds.
facts.quote: Apple Maps pulls from a combination of its own data and Yelp feeds.

facts.fact: Third-party source BrightLocal's annual Local Search Ranking Factors survey consistently identifies citation signals as one of the top factors influencing local pack rankings (no numeric value given).

facts.fact: The page cites the Whitespark 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors report as reinforcing that citation consistency is what makes citations effective (no numeric value given).
